title: US looks to expand use of canoe-sized drones to deter migrant crossings
key_facts: The Pentagon is considering expanding its fleet of autonomous surveillance boats on the Rio Grande from 10 vessels by as many as 50 boats, after a pilot programme, Reuters reported.
The boats are Lightfish unmanned surface vessels from San Diego firm Seasats: 11 feet long, 340 pounds, solar-powered.
They can stay out up to six months without refuelling or maintenance and carry electro-optical, infrared and sonar sensors.
The Pentagon told Reuters that in an average month the boats have assisted with 452 detections, 350 apprehensions and 100 turnbacks.
Officials are studying use in the Gulf of Mexico, possibly a wider network between Texas and Florida, and later tests in the Pacific near San Diego.
Data can feed systems used by Customs and Border Protection and the Coast Guard.
For now the Pentagon is studying an expansion rather than committing to full deployment.

why_it_matters_hint: Cheap, long-endurance robot boats could become a standing part of border and sea surveillance if the Pentagon expands the pilot.
event_date: Reuters report 2 Oct 2026; pilot launched earlier (article says January)
notes: Reuters (original, HTTP 401) could not be read; written from Outlook India, which summarises the Reuters report. Reuters photo caption (via Lufkin Daily News) confirms the Lightfish boat off Texas, 30 Jul 2026. The "detections, apprehensions, turnbacks" figures are the Pentagon’s own and not independently checked. Article does not give the pilot year.
